original:
Let $p\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ be prime, let $d\geq 4$ be even, and assume
 $p\nmid 2d$ . Then $\mathcal{H}_{d}$ is maximal over some finite extension of
 $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ if and only if one of the following holds:

(1) 

 $d=4$ and $p\equiv 5\pmod{8}$ ;

(2) 

 $d=2\ell^{a}$ , where $\ell\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ is prime, $a\geq 1$ , and
 $p$ generates $(\mathbb{Z}/\ell^{a}\mathbb{Z})^{\times}$ .

In case (1), the maximal fields are precisely $\mathbb{F}_{p^{2b}}$ with
 $b$ positive and odd. In case (2), if
 $M=\ell^{a-1}(\ell-1)$ , they are precisely $\mathbb{F}_{p^{Mb}}$ with $b$ 
positive and odd.
